      { key: 'swingLow', type: 'line', title: 'Swing Low', style: { color: L_COLOR, visible: false } },
    ],

    calc(bars, settings, store, ctx) {
      const n = bars.length
      const blank = () => new Array(n).fill(NaN)

      const columns = {
        swingHigh: blank(),
        swingLow: blank(),
        labelPrecision: blank(),
        eqHighLeft: blank(),
        eqHighRight: blank(),
        eqHighTop: blank(),
        eqHighBottom: blank(),
        eqLowLeft: blank(),
        eqLowRight: blank(),
        eqLowTop: blank(),
        eqLowBottom: blank(),
      }
      for (const defaults of GROUP_DEFAULTS) {
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}HighLevel`] = blank()
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}HighX1`] = blank()
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}HighX2`] = blank()
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}LowLevel`] = blank()
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}LowX1`] = blank()
        columns[`${defaults.prefix}LowX2`] = blank()
      }

      const finish = () => {
        const result = {}
        for (const key of Object.keys(columns)) result[key] = nulls(columns[key])
        return result
      }

      if (n === 0) return finish()

      const zone = resolveZone(ctx)

      // The label text is the level itself, so it is formatted to the
      // instrument's own tick rather than to a fixed number of decimals. The
      // draws hook never sees ctx, which is why the precision travels as a
      // column. A host that has not set minMove leaves it unavailable and the
      // hook falls back to the magnitude of the number.
      const tick = Number(ctx && ctx.tickSize) // 0
      if (tick > 0) {
        const decimals = precisionForStep(tick)
        if (Number.isFinite(decimals)) columns.labelPrecision.fill(decimals)
      }

      // float _high = source == 'Open/Close' ? math.max(open, close) : high
      const useBody = String(settings.source ?? 'High/Low') === 'Open/Close'
      const srcHigh = new Array(n)
      const srcLow = new Array(n)
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        srcHigh[i] = useBody ? Math.max(bar.open, bar.close) : bar.high
        srcLow[i] = useBody ? Math.min(bar.open, bar.close) : bar.low
      }

      /**
       * f_offsetToP: walk back over the chart's own source series for the bar
       * whose value sits closest to the higher timeframe pivot price, which is
       * the bar that actually made the swing. The comparison is strict, so the
       * nearest bar wins a tie, and the search starts one bar back exactly as
       * the source does.
       */
      const offsetToP = (series, price, maxBack, at) => {
        if (!Number.isFinite(price)) return NaN
        let delta = 10e10
        let offset = NaN
        for (let j = 1; j <= maxBack; j++) {
          const index = at - j
          if (index < 0) break
          const thisDelta = Math.abs(series[index] - price)
          if (Number.isFinite(thisDelta) && thisDelta < delta) {
            delta = thisDelta
            offset = j
          }
        }
        return offset
      }

      /**
       * f_extendArray: a level is carried one bar at a time for as long as the
       * new bar does not trade through it. The first bar whose raw high is
       * above the level and whose raw low is below it takes that liquidity, and
       * the line stops there for good. 'Line Extend' overrides the whole test
       * and runs every level to the last bar.
       */
      const extendTo = (at, level, always) => {
        if (always) return n - 1
        let x2 = at
        for (let k = at + 1; k < n; k++) {
          const bar = bars[k]
          if (bar.high > level && bar.low < level) break
          x2 = k
        }
        return x2
      }

      /* ------------------------------------- pivot high low 1, 2 and 3 */

      for (const defaults of GROUP_DEFAULTS) {
        const cfg = readGroup(settings, defaults.prefix, defaults)
        if (!cfg.show // cfg.showLast === 0) continue

        const htf = foldHigherTimeframe(bars, parseTimeframe(cfg.tf), zone)
        if (htf.length === 0) continue

        const htfHigh = new Array(htf.length)
        const htfLow = new Array(htf.length)
        for (let k = 0; k < htf.length; k++) {
          const hb = htf[k]
          htfHigh[k] = useBody ? Math.max(hb.open, hb.close) : hb.high
          htfLow[k] = useBody ? Math.min(hb.open, hb.close) : hb.low
        }

        const pivotH = pivotHigh(htfHigh, cfg.left, cfg.right)
        const pivotL = pivotLow(htfLow, cfg.left, cfg.right)

        const bucket = new Array(n).fill(-1)
        for (let k = 0; k < htf.length; k++) {
          for (let i = htf[k].from; i <= htf[k].to; i++) bucket[i] = k
        }

        // request.security with lookahead_off hands over the last COMPLETED
        // higher timeframe bar, so a fold coarser than the chart is read one
        // bucket behind. A requested timeframe at or below the chart's own
        // folds one chart bar per bucket and is read without that lag, which is
        // what request.security returns when the two timeframes match.
        const lag = htf.length === n ? 0 : 1

        // int(f_tfResInMinutes(tf) / res_in_minutes): the number of chart bars
        // in one higher timeframe bar, measured off the fold so a session
        // bounded instrument is not counted as if it traded around the clock.
        const barsHtf = Math.max(1, Math.round(n / htf.length))
        const barsOffset = Math.floor(cfg.left * barsHtf)
        if (barsOffset > MAX_BARS_BACK) continue
        const maxBack = Math.min(MAX_BARS_BACK, Math.max(30, barsOffset + barsHtf + 1))

        // na(series[1]) and not na(series): the level is drawn once, on the
        // chart bar where the higher timeframe pivot first becomes available.
        // Two higher timeframe bars pivoting back to back therefore draw one
        // level, not two, which is the source's behaviour.
        const events = []
        let previousHigh = NaN
        let previousLow = NaN
        for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
          const k = bucket[i] - lag
          const currentHigh = k >= 0 ? pivotH[k] : NaN
          const currentLow = k >= 0 ? pivotL[k] : NaN
          if (!Number.isFinite(previousHigh) && Number.isFinite(currentHigh)) {
            events.push({ at: i, side: 'High', price: currentHigh })
          }
          if (!Number.isFinite(previousLow) && Number.isFinite(currentLow)) {
            events.push({ at: i, side: 'Low', price: currentLow })
          }
          previousHigh = currentHigh
          previousLow = currentLow
        }

        // One array holds both the highs and the lows in the source, and the
        // oldest line is deleted once it is full, so the cap counts them
        // together rather than per side.
        const kept = events.length > cfg.showLast ? events.slice(events.length - cfg.showLast) : events

        for (const event of kept) {
          const series = event.side === 'High' ? srcHigh : srcLow
          const offset = offsetToP(series, event.price, maxBack, event.at)
          if (!Number.isFinite(offset)) continue
          const x1 = event.at - offset
          if (x1 < 0) continue
          columns[`${defaults.prefix}${event.side}Level`][event.at] = event.price
          columns[`${defaults.prefix}${event.side}X1`][event.at] = x1
          columns[`${defaults.prefix}${event.side}X2`][event.at] = extendTo(event.at, event.price, cfg.extend)
        }
      }

      /* ---------------------------------------------- equal high and low */

      const eqLeft = intInput(settings.eqLeft, 60, 1, 1000)
      const eqRight = intInput(settings.eqRight, 30, 1, 1000)
      const eqPercent = floatInput(settings.eqPercent, 0.05, 0, 100)
      const eqShow = settings.phlEqShow !== false

      // The source requests these on timeframe '', which is the chart itself,
      // so there is nothing to fold here.
      const eqPivotHigh = pivotHigh(srcHigh, eqLeft, eqRight)
      const eqPivotLow = pivotLow(srcLow, eqLeft, eqRight)
      columns.swingHigh = eqPivotHigh.slice()
      columns.swingLow = eqPivotLow.slice()

      let highPrice0 = NaN
      let highPrice1 = NaN
      let highBar0 = NaN
      let highBar1 = NaN
      let lowPrice0 = NaN
      let lowPrice1 = NaN
      let lowBar0 = NaN
      let lowBar1 = NaN

      // pchg: the gap between the last two swings of the same kind, as a
      // percentage of the older one.
      const percentChange = (a, b) => {
        if (!Number.isFinite(a) // !Number.isFinite(b) // b === 0) return NaN
        return Math.abs(((a - b) / b) * 100)
      }

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const hasHigh = Number.isFinite(eqPivotHigh[i])
        const hasLow = Number.isFinite(eqPivotLow[i])

        if (hasHigh) {
          highBar1 = highBar0
          highBar0 = i
          highPrice1 = highPrice0
          highPrice0 = eqPivotHigh[i]
        }
        if (hasLow) {
          lowBar1 = lowBar0
          lowBar0 = i
          lowPrice1 = lowPrice0
          lowPrice0 = eqPivotLow[i]
        }

        if (!eqShow) continue

        if (hasHigh) {
          const pchg = percentChange(highPrice0, highPrice1)
          // Pine treats every comparison against an unavailable value as
          // false, so the very first swing, which has nothing to compare
          // against, must not box itself.
          if (Number.isFinite(pchg) && pchg < eqPercent) {
            const left = highBar1 - eqRight
            const right = highBar0 - eqRight
            if (Number.isFinite(left) && left >= 0 && right >= 0 && right < n) {
              columns.eqHighLeft[i] = left
              columns.eqHighRight[i] = right
              columns.eqHighTop[i] = highPrice1
              columns.eqHighBottom[i] = highPrice0
            }
          }
        }

        if (hasLow) {
          const pchg = percentChange(lowPrice0, lowPrice1)
          if (Number.isFinite(pchg) && pchg < eqPercent) {
            const left = lowBar1 - eqRight
            const right = lowBar0 - eqRight
            if (Number.isFinite(left) && left >= 0 && right >= 0 && right < n) {
              columns.eqLowLeft[i] = left
              columns.eqLowRight[i] = right
              columns.eqLowTop[i] = lowPrice1
              columns.eqLowBottom[i] = lowPrice0
            }
          }
        }
      }

      return finish()
    },

    markers({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const n = bars.length
      if (n === 0) return []
      if (settings.phlEqShow === false) return []

      const transparency = intInput(settings.eqTransp, 25, 0, 100)
      const opacity = (100 - transparency) / 100
      const highColor = withAlpha(H_COLOR, opacity)
      const lowColor = withAlpha(L_COLOR, opacity)

      const out = []
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        // plotshape(..., location.absolute, offset=-right) puts the mark on the
        // swing bar itself, at that bar's raw high or low. xcross is not in the
        // marker shape set, so a diamond stands in for it.
        const highBar = values.eqHighRight[i]
        if (Number.isFinite(highBar) && highBar >= 0 && highBar < n) {
          out.push({
            time: bars[highBar].time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bars[highBar].high,
            shape: 'diamond',
            size: 'small',
            color: highColor,
          })
        }
        const lowBar = values.eqLowRight[i]
        if (Number.isFinite(lowBar) && lowBar >= 0 && lowBar < n) {
          out.push({
            time: bars[lowBar].time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bars[lowBar].low,
            shape: 'diamond',
            size: 'small',
            color: lowColor,
          })
        }
      }
      return out
    },

    draws({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const n = bars.length
      if (n === 0) return []

      // bar_index anchors become bar times: paging older history in shifts
      // every index, and a level welded to an index would slide off its swing.
      const timeAt = (index) => {
        if (!Number.isFinite(index)) return NaN
        const k = Math.round(index)
        if (k < 0 // k >= n) return NaN
        return bars[k].time
      }

      // str.tostring(price) for the level labels. The instrument's own tick
      // decides the decimals when the host has published one; otherwise the
      // magnitude of the number does.
      const precision = values.labelPrecision[0]
      const formatPrice = (value) => {
        if (!Number.isFinite(value)) return ''
        let decimals
        if (Number.isFinite(precision)) {
          decimals = Math.min(10, Math.max(0, Math.round(precision)))
        } else {
          const magnitude = Math.abs(value)
          decimals = magnitude >= 1000 ? 2 : magnitude >= 1 ? 4 : 6
        }
        return String(Number(value.toFixed(decimals)))
      }

      const out = []

      for (const defaults of GROUP_DEFAULTS) {
        const cfg = readGroup(settings, defaults.prefix, defaults)
        if (!cfg.show // cfg.showLast === 0) continue

        for (const side of ['High', 'Low']) {
          const levels = values[`${defaults.prefix}${side}Level`]
          const starts = values[`${defaults.prefix}${side}X1`]
          const ends = values[`${defaults.prefix}${side}X2`]
          const color = side === 'High' ? H_COLOR : L_COLOR

          for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            const level = levels[i]
            if (!Number.isFinite(level)) continue
            const from = timeAt(starts[i])
            const to = timeAt(ends[i])
            if (!Number.isFinite(from) // !Number.isFinite(to)) continue

            out.push({
              kind: 'line',
              from: { time: from, price: level },
              to: { time: to, price: level },
              color,
              lineWidth: cfg.lineWidth,
              lineStyle: cfg.lineStyle,
            })

            if (cfg.labelShow) {
              // The label is created at the left end and moved to the right end
              // on every bar the line extends, so it sits at the right end of
              // any level that ever extended and at the left end of one that
              // never did. Pine pads the text with spaces to push it clear of
              // the anchor; align does that here.
              const extended = Math.round(ends[i]) > i
              const anchor = extended ? to : from
              out.push({
                kind: 'label',
                at: { time: anchor, price: level },
                text: formatPrice(level),
                color: withAlpha('#000000', 0),
                textColor: color,
                align: 'left',
              })
            }
          }
        }
      }

      if (settings.phlEqShow !== false) {
        const transparency = intInput(settings.eqTransp, 25, 0, 100)
        const opacity = (100 - transparency) / 100
        // The source never trims its box array, so the platform ceiling of 50
        // decides which survive. Newest first, so the ones a trader is looking
        // at are the ones that are kept.
        const boxes = []
        for (let i = n - 1; i >= 0 && boxes.length < MAX_EQUAL_BOXES; i--) {
          const highLeft = timeAt(values.eqHighLeft[i])
          const highRight = timeAt(values.eqHighRight[i])
          if (Number.isFinite(highLeft) && Number.isFinite(highRight)) {
            boxes.push({
              kind: 'box',
              from: { time: highLeft, price: values.eqHighTop[i] },
              to: { time: highRight, price: values.eqHighBottom[i] },
              color: withAlpha(H_COLOR, opacity),
              fillColor: H_COLOR,
              opacity,
            })
          }
          if (boxes.length >= MAX_EQUAL_BOXES) break
          const lowLeft = timeAt(values.eqLowLeft[i])
          const lowRight = timeAt(values.eqLowRight[i])
          if (Number.isFinite(lowLeft) && Number.isFinite(lowRight)) {
            boxes.push({
              kind: 'box | `oa-ict-external-range-liquidity-static-multi-timeframe-swing-hi` | `oa-ict-external-range-liquidity-static-multi-timeframe-swing-hi.js` | [source](https://github.com/ArunKBhaskar/PineScript/blob/c6821225c466494b01eee08f9dd88bf84d2b24ba/ICT) |
| ICT Fair Value Gap (FVG) Scanner v2',
    category: 'ICT',
    placement: 'onchart',

    inputs: [
      {
        key: 'method',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Scanning Method',
        default: METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF,
        group: 'Scanner',
        tooltip: 'Which stage of the gap the scan reports. The source draws nothing on the chart for FVG %: that stage was reported only through its multi-symbol screener table, which a chart study cannot reach.',
        options: [
          { label: 'FVG %', value: METHOD_FVG_PCT },
          { label: 'First Touch', value: METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH },
          { label: 'First Touch Confirmed', value: METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF },
          { label: 'Full Fill', value: METHOD_FULL_FILL },
          { label: 'Full Fill Confirmed', value: METHOD_FULL_FILL_CONF },
          { label: 'Reversal', value: METHOD_REVERSAL },
        ],
      },
      { key: 'showLong', type: 'boolean', label: 'Long Signals', default: true, group: 'Scanner' },
      { key: 'showShort', type: 'boolean', label: 'Short Signals', default: true, group: 'Scanner' },

      { key: 'closeGapsPartially', type: 'boolean', label: 'Close FVG Partially', default: true, group: 'FVG' },
      { key: 'boxLimit', type: 'number', label: 'Max Number of FVG', default: 15, min: 1, max: 500, step: 1, group: 'FVG' },
      {
        key: 'minimalDeviation',
        type: 'number',
        label: 'Minimal Deviation (%)',
        default: 70,
        min: 1,
        max: 100,
        step: 1,
        group: 'FVG',
        tooltip: 'Smallest gap that counts, as a percentage of the average high-low range of the last 14 bars. If no gap is ever found, either this is set too high or the feed aligns every bar open to the previous close.',
      },
      {
        key: 'limitBoxLength',
        type: 'boolean',
        label: 'Max Bars',
        default: false,
        group: 'FVG',
        tooltip: 'Stop trailing a gap once it has run this many bars, whether or not price filled it.',
      },
      { key: 'limitBoxLengthBars', type: 'number', label: 'Max Gap Trail Length (bars)', default: 300, min: 1, max: 5000, step: 1, group: 'FVG' },
      {
        key: 'transparency',
        type: 'number',
        label: 'Transp',
        default: 70,
        min: 0,
        max: 100,
        step: 1,
        group: 'FVG',
        tooltip: 'Transparency of the gap boxes, as in the source. The border is drawn 20 points more transparent than the fill.',
      },

      {

        type: 'boolean',

        default: false,

      },
      { key: 'hourFrom', type: 'number', label: 'Time From (hour)', default: 9, min: 0, max: 23, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'minuteFrom', type: 'number', label: 'Time From (minute)', default: 15, min: 0, max: 59, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'hourTo', type: 'number', label: 'Time To (hour)', default: 10, min: 0, max: 23, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'minuteTo', type: 'number', label: 'Time To (minute)', default: 15, min: 0, max: 59, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'dateFilter', type: 'boolean', label: 'Apply Date Filter', default: false, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'day', type: 'number', label: 'Day', default: 25, min: 1, max: 31, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'month', type: 'number', label: 'Month', default: 10, min: 1, max: 12, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'year', type: 'number', label: 'Year', default: 2024, min: 0, max: 9999, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },

      { key: 'showTable', type: 'boolean', label: 'Display Table', default: true, group: 'Data Table' },
      {
        key: 'tablePosition',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Position',
        default: 'bottom-right',
        group: 'Data Table',
        options: [
          { label: 'Top Left', value: 'top-left' },
          { label: 'Top Center', value: 'top-center' },
          { label: 'Top Right', value: 'top-right' },
          { label: 'Middle Left', value: 'middle-left' },
          { label: 'Middle Center', value: 'middle-center' },
          { label: 'Middle Right', value: 'middle-right' },
          { label: 'Bottom Left', value: 'bottom-left' },
          { label: 'Bottom Center', value: 'bottom-center' },
          { label: 'Bottom Right', value: 'bottom-right' },
        ],
      },
      {
        key: 'tableSize',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Size',
        default: 'normal',
        group: 'Data Table',
        options: [
          { label: 'Tiny', value: 'tiny' },
          { label: 'Small', value: 'small' },
          { label: 'Normal', value: 'normal' },
          { label: 'Large', value: 'large' },
          { label: 'Huge', value: 'huge' },
        ],
      },
    ],

    // The four series the source plots, all with display.none: they carry the
    // live gap edges into the legend and the crosshair without drawing a line.
    plots: [
      { key: 'fvgDownTop', type: 'line', title: 'FVG Down Top', style: { color: NEG, visible: false } },
      { key: 'fvgDownBottom', type: 'line', title: 'FVG Down Bottom', style: { color: NEG, visible: false } },
      { key: 'fvgUpTop', type: 'line', title: 'FVG Up Top', style: { color: POS, visible: false } },
      { key: 'fvgUpBottom', type: 'line', title: 'FVG Up Bottom', style: { color: POS, visible: false } },
    ],

    calc(bars, settings, store, ctx) {
      const n = bars.length
      const cfg = readConfig(settings)
      const method = String(settings.method ?? METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF)

      // Bar times are UTC seconds while Pine's hour and dayofmonth are exchange
      // wall clock, so the browser's local time would compute a different chart
      // in every city.
      const zoneCandidate = ctx && typeof ctx.timezone === 'string' ? ctx.timezone : ''
      const zone = zoneCandidate && isValidTimezone(zoneCandidate) ? zoneCandidate : DEFAULT_TIMEZONE

      // barstate.isconfirmed: every historical bar is closed, and the last one
      // is closed only when the host says so.
      const lastUnconfirmed = ctx && ctx.barState ? ctx.barState.isConfirmed === false : false

      const { isDown, isUp, gaps } = detectGaps(bars, cfg)

      const hourFrom = clamp(int(settings.hourFrom, 9), 0, 23)
      const minuteFrom = clamp(int(settings.minuteFrom, 15), 0, 59)
      const hourTo = clamp(int(settings.hourTo, 10), 0, 23)
      const minuteTo = clamp(int(settings.minuteTo, 15), 0, 59)
      const wantDay = clamp(int(settings.day, 25), 1, 31)
      const wantMonth = clamp(int(settings.month, 10), 1, 12)
      const wantYear = Math.max(0, int(settings.year, 2024))
      const useTimeFilter = settings.timeFilter === true
      const useDateFilter = settings.dateFilter === true

      const fvgDownTop = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const fvgDownBottom = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const fvgUpTop = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const fvgUpBottom = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const fvgDownPercent = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const fvgUpPercent = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumPchgCol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumVolCol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const prevCumVolCol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumVolPchgCol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const signalShort = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const signalLong = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const gapCount = new Array(n).fill(gaps.length)

      // Every `var` in the source is one of these: a value that survives the
      // bar it was written on until something overwrites it.
      let dTop = NaN
      let dBottom = NaN
      let dPercent = NaN
      let uTop = NaN
      let uBottom = NaN
      let uPercent = NaN
      let cumPchg = NaN
      let curCumVol = NaN
      let prevCumVol = NaN
      let s2low = NaN
      let s3low = NaN
      let l2high = NaN
      let l3high = NaN
      let sFirstTouch = 0
      let sFirstTouchConf = 0
      let sFullFill = 0
      let sFullFillConf = 0
      let sReversal = 0
      let lFirstTouch = 0
      let lFirstTouchConf = 0
      let lFullFill = 0
      let lFullFillConf = 0
      let lReversal = 0
      let prevDayIndex = NaN

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        const prevBar = i > 0 ? bars[i - 1] : null
        const prevHigh = prevBar ? prevBar.high : NaN
        const prevLow = prevBar ? prevBar.low : NaN
        const prevClose = prevBar ? prevBar.close : NaN

        // What each var series carried at the close of the previous bar.
        // ta.crossover needs it, and it has to be read before this bar writes.
        const pDTop = dTop
        const pDBottom = dBottom
        const pUTop = uTop
        const pUBottom = uBottom
        const pS2low = s2low
        const pS3low = s3low
        const pL2high = l2high
        const pL3high = l3high

        // ta.change(time('D')) != 0. Pine's change is na on the first bar and a
        // comparison with na is false, so bar 0 never counts as a new day.
        const dayIndex = zonedDayIndex(bar.time, zone)
        const isNewDay = i > 0 && dayIndex !== prevDayIndex
        prevDayIndex = dayIndex

        // Cumulative percentage change, reset every session.
        const dailyPct =
          prevBar && Number.isFinite(prevBar.close) && prevBar.close !== 0 && Number.isFinite(bar.close)
            ? ((bar.close - prevBar.close) / prevBar.close) * 100
            : 0
        cumPchg = isNewDay ? dailyPct : !Number.isFinite(cumPchg) ? dailyPct : cumPchg + dailyPct

        // Cumulative volume. Index series carry no volume at all, and the
        // source's `na + volume` is na, so an absent figure stays absent rather
        // than being reported as zero traded.
        const vol = Number.isFinite(bar.volume) ? bar.volume : NaN
        if (isNewDay) {
          prevCumVol = curCumVol
          curCumVol = vol
        } else {
          curCumVol = curCumVol + vol
        }
        const volBase = Number.isFinite(prevCumVol) ? prevCumVol : curCumVol
        const cumVolPchg =
          Number.isFinite(volBase) && volBase !== 0 && Number.isFinite(curCumVol)
            ? ((curCumVol - volBase) / volBase) * 100
            : NaN

        // The only two filters the source's signal conditions actually read.
        const parts = utcSecondsToZonedParts(bar.time, zone)
        let timeOk = true
        if (useTimeFilter) {
          const h = parts.hour
          const m = parts.minute
          timeOk =
            (h > hourFrom // (h === hourFrom && m >= minuteFrom)) &&
            (h < hourTo // (h === hourTo && m < minuteTo))
        }
        let dateOk = true
        if (useDateFilter) {
          dateOk = parts.year === wantYear && parts.month === wantMonth && parts.day === wantDay
        }
        const confirmed = !(lastUnconfirmed && i === n - 1)
        const gate = timeOk && dateOk && confirmed

        // The var gap edges, written before the signal block reads them, which
        // is why a gap can never trigger its own touch on its own bar.
        if (isDown[i]) {
          const top = bars[i - 2].low
          dTop = top
          dBottom = bar.high
          dPercent = Number.isFinite(top) && top !== 0 ? ((top - bar.high) / top) * 100 : NaN
        }
        if (isUp[i]) {
          const bottom = bars[i - 2].high
          uTop = bar.low
          uBottom = bottom
          uPercent = Number.isFinite(bottom) && bottom !== 0 ? ((bar.low - bottom) / bottom) * 100 : NaN
        }

        // Short side: a down gap sits above price, so filling it is a rally.
        const sc1 = isDown[i] && gate
        const sc2 = gate && crossOver(prevHigh, bar.high, pDBottom, dBottom)
        if (sc2) s2low = bar.low
        const sc2conf = gate && crossUnder(prevClose, bar.close, pS2low, s2low)
        const sc3 =
          gate && crossOver(prevHigh, bar.high, pDTop, dTop) &&
          Number.isFinite(dTop) && bar.close < dTop
        if (sc3) s3low = bar.low
        const sc3conf = gate && crossUnder(prevClose, bar.close, pS3low, s3low)
        const sc4 = gate && crossOver(prevClose, bar.close, pDTop, dTop)

        // Long side: an up gap sits below price, so filling it is a decline.
        const lc1 = isUp[i] && gate
        const lc2 = gate && crossUnder(prevLow, bar.low, pUTop, uTop)
        if (lc2) l2high = bar.high
        const lc2conf = gate && crossOver(prevClose, bar.close, pL2high, l2high)
        const lc3 =
          gate && crossUnder(prevLow, bar.low, pUBottom, uBottom) &&
          Number.isFinite(uBottom) && bar.close > uBottom
        if (lc3) l3high = bar.high
        const lc3conf = gate && crossOver(prevClose, bar.close, pL3high, l3high)
        const lc4 = gate && crossUnder(prevClose, bar.close, pUBottom, uBottom)

        sFirstTouch = step2(sFirstTouch, sc1, sc2)
        sFirstTouchConf = step3(sFirstTouchConf, sc1, sc2, sc2conf)
        sFullFill = step2(sFullFill, sc1, sc3)
        sFullFillConf = step3(sFullFillConf, sc1, sc3, sc3conf)
        sReversal = step2(sReversal, sc1, sc4)

        lFirstTouch = step2(lFirstTouch, lc1, lc2)
        lFirstTouchConf = step3(lFirstTouchConf, lc1, lc2, lc2conf)
        lFullFill = step2(lFullFill, lc1, lc3)
        lFullFillConf = step3(lFullFillConf, lc1, lc3, lc3conf)
        lReversal = step2(lReversal, lc1, lc4)

        let shortCond
        let longCond
        switch (method) {
          case METHOD_FVG_PCT:
            shortCond = sc1
            longCond = lc1
            break
          case METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH:
            shortCond = sFirstTouch === 2
            longCond = lFirstTouch === 2
            break
          case METHOD_FULL_FILL:
            shortCond = sFullFill === 2
            longCond = lFullFill === 2
            break
          case METHOD_FULL_FILL_CONF:
            shortCond = sFullFillConf === 3
            longCond = lFullFillConf === 3
            break
          case METHOD_REVERSAL:
            shortCond = sReversal === 2
            longCond = lReversal === 2
            break
          default:
            shortCond = sFirstTouchConf === 3
            longCond = lFirstTouchConf === 3
        }

        fvgDownTop[i] = dTop
        fvgDownBottom[i] = dBottom
        fvgUpTop[i] = uTop
        fvgUpBottom[i] = uBottom
        fvgDownPercent[i] = dPercent
        fvgUpPercent[i] = uPercent
        cumPchgCol[i] = cumPchg
        cumVolCol[i] = curCumVol
        prevCumVolCol[i] = prevCumVol
        cumVolPchgCol[i] = cumVolPchg
        if (shortCond) signalShort[i] = 1
        if (longCond) signalLong[i] = 1
      }

      return {
        fvgDownTop: nulls(fvgDownTop),
        fvgDownBottom: nulls(fvgDownBottom),
        fvgUpTop: nulls(fvgUpTop),
        fvgUpBottom: nulls(fvgUpBottom),
        fvgDownPercent: nulls(fvgDownPercent),
        fvgUpPercent: nulls(fvgUpPercent),
        cumPchg: nulls(cumPchgCol),
        cumVol: nulls(cumVolCol),
        prevCumVol: nulls(prevCumVolCol),
        cumVolPchg: nulls(cumVolPchgCol),
        signalShort: nulls(signalShort),
        signalLong: nulls(signalLong),
        gapCount,
      }
    },

    // box.new, box.set_right and box.delete. A gap still being trailed runs to
    // the last bar: extend.right carries on into the empty space past the data,
    // which has no bar to anchor to here.
    draws({ bars, settings }) {
      if (bars.length === 0) return []
      const cfg = readConfig(settings)
      const { gaps } = detectGaps(bars, cfg)
      const lastIndex = bars.length - 1
      const fillAlpha = (100 - cfg.transp) / 100
      const borderAlpha = Math.max(0, 100 - (cfg.transp + ADD_TRANSP)) / 100
      const out = []

      for (const gap of gaps) {
        const colour = gap.isDown ? NEG : POS
        for (const box of gap.boxes) {
          if (box.deleted) continue
          if (!Number.isFinite(box.top) // !Number.isFinite(box.bottom)) continue
          const leftIndex = clamp(box.left, 0, lastIndex)
          const rightIndex = clamp(box.extend ? lastIndex : box.right, 0, lastIndex)
          out.push({
            kind: 'box',
            from: { time: bars[leftIndex].time, price: box.top },
            to: { time: bars[rightIndex].time, price: box.bottom },
            color: withAlpha(colour, borderAlpha),
            fillColor: colour,
            opacity: fillAlpha,
          })
        }
      }
      return out
    },

    // plotchar and plotshape. The source draws nothing for the FVG % stage:
    // that one reported only through the multi-symbol screener table.
    //
    // aboveBar and belowBar resolve against this indicator's own series, which
    // here is a hidden gap edge, so the anchors are explicit prices.
    markers({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const method = String(settings.method ?? METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF)
      if (method === METHOD_FVG_PCT) return []
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      if (!showShort && !showLong) return []

      // Reversal is the one stage the source flips: a short-side reversal is
      // price closing back above a bearish gap, which is a bullish event, so it
      // is drawn below the bar in the positive colour and the long side above.
      const flipped = method === METHOD_REVERSAL
      const shortShape = flipped ? 'triangleUp' : 'triangleDown'
      const longShape = flipped ? 'triangleDown' : 'triangleUp'
      const shortColour = flipped ? POS_LIGHT : NEG_LIGHT
      const longColour = flipped ? NEG_LIGHT : POS_LIGHT

      const pad = markerPad(bars)
      const out = []
      for (let i = 0; i < bars.length; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        if (showShort && values.signalShort[i] != null) {
          const price = flipped ? bar.low - pad : bar.high + pad
          if (Number.isFinite(price)) {
            out.push({ time: bar.time, position: 'atPrice', price, shape: shortShape, color: shortColour, size: 'tiny' })
          }
        }
        if (showLong && values.signalLong[i] != null) {
          const price = flipped ? bar.high + pad : bar.low - pad
          if (Number.isFinite(price)) {
            out.push({ time: bar.time, position: 'atPrice', price, shape: longShape, color: longColour, size: 'tiny' })
          }
        }
      }
      return out
    },

    // barcolor(). The source pairs the short side with the negative colour on
    // the two touch stages and with the positive colour on the two fill stages
    // and the reversal; that asymmetry is carried over as written.
    barColors({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const method = String(settings.method ?? METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF)
      const out = new Array(bars.length).fill(null)
      if (method === METHOD_FVG_PCT) return out
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      const touchStage = method === METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH // method === METHOD_FIRST_TOUCH_CONF
      const shortColour = touchStage ? NEG_LIGHT : POS_LIGHT
      const longColour = touchStage ? POS_LIGHT : NEG_LIGHT

      for (let i = 0; i < bars.length; i++) {
        if (showShort && values.signalShort[i] != null) out[i] = shortColour
        else if (showLong && values.signalLong[i] != null) out[i] = longColour
      }
      return out
    },

    // The source's own four-row data table, which it draws only on the last
    // bar, which is all this hook is ever asked for.
    table({ bars, values, settings }) {
      if (settings.showTable === false // bars.length === 0) return null
      const i = bars.length - 1
      const pchg = values.cumPchg[i]
      const volPchg = values.cumVolPchg[i]
      const curVol = values.cumVol[i]
      const prevVol = values.prevCumVol[i]
      const noGaps = values.gapCount[i] === 0

      const pchgColour = Number.isFinite(pchg) && pchg > 0 ? POS : NEG
      const volPchgColour = Number.isFinite(volPchg) && volPchg > 0 ? POS : NEG
      const prevVolColour =
        Number.isFinite(prevVol) && Number.isFinite(curVol) && prevVol < curVol ? NEG : POS

      const lakh = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? `${fmt2(v / 100000)} L` : '-')
      const pct = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? `${fmt2(v)} %` : '-')

      const label = (text, bg) => ({ text, textColor: NEU, bgColor: bg, align: 'left' })
      const value = (text, colour, bg) => ({ text, textColor: colour, bgColor: bg, align: 'right' })

      const rows = [
        [label('%Chg', NEU_DARK), value(pct(pchg), pchgColour, NEU_DARK)],
        [label('Vol %Chg', NEU_MID), value(pct(volPchg), volPchgColour, NEU_MID)],
        [label('Vol', NEU_DARK), value(lakh(curVol), volPchgColour, NEU_DARK)],
        [label('PD Vol', NEU_MID), value(lakh(prevVol), prevVolColour, NEU_MID)],
      ]
      // The source pops a separate note when the chart holds no gap at all.
      if (noGaps) rows.push([label('FVG', NEU_DARK), value('None found', NEU, NEU_DARK)])

      const size = String(settings.tableSize ?? 'normal')
      return {
        rows,
        options: {
          position: String(settings.tablePosition ?? 'bottom-right | `oa-ict-fair-value-gap-fvg-scanner` | `oa-ict-fair-value-gap-fvg-scanner.js` | [source](https://github.com/ArunKBhaskar/PineScript/blob/c6821225c466494b01eee08f9dd88bf84d2b24ba/ICT) |
| ICT Liquidity Sweep Pattern Scanner',
    category: 'ICT',
    placement: 'onchart',

    inputs: [
      {
        key: 'method',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Screening Method',
        default: 'Prev 2 Swing Sweep',
        group: 'Scanner',
        options: METHODS.map((m) => ({ label: m, value: m })),
        tooltip: 'Which earlier swing the newest swing has to sweep: the 1st, 2nd or 3rd one back.',
      },
      { key: 'showLong', type: 'boolean', label: 'Long Signals', default: true, group: 'Scanner' },
      { key: 'showShort', type: 'boolean', label: 'Short Signals', default: true, group: 'Scanner' },

      { key: 'showZigzag', type: 'boolean', label: 'Display Zig Zag', default: true, group: 'Zig Zag' },
      { key: 'zzPeriod', type: 'number', label: 'Zig Zag Length', default: 4, min: 2, max: 500, step: 1, group: 'Zig Zag' },
      {
        key: 'zzSource',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Source',
        default: 'High/Low',
        group: 'Zig Zag',
        options: [
          { label: 'High/Low', value: 'High/Low' },
          { label: 'Open/Close', value: 'Open/Close' },
        ],
      },
      {
        key: 'levelLineStyle',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Swept Level Line Style',
        default: 'solid',
        group: 'Zig Zag',
        options: [
          { label: 'Solid', value: 'solid' },
          { label: 'Dashed', value: 'dashed' },
          { label: 'Dotted', value: 'dotted' },
        ],
        tooltip: 'Style of the line drawn from the swept swing across to the signal bar.',
      },

      { key: 'showDataTable', type: 'boolean', label: 'Display Table', default: true, group: 'Data Table' },
      {
        key: 'tablePosition',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Position',
        default: 'bottom-right',
        group: 'Data Table',
        options: TABLE_POSITIONS.map((p) => ({ label: p.replace('-', ' '), value: p })),
      },
      {
        key: 'tableSize',
        type: 'select',
        label: 'Size',
        default: 'normal',
        group: 'Data Table',
        options: Object.keys(FONT_SIZES).map((k) => ({ label: k, value: k })),
      },
    ],

    // The source has no plot() at all: the zig zag is a run of line.new calls
    // joining consecutive swing points. One column carrying the straight-line
    // value between each pair of points draws the same polyline, and gives the
    // leg a colour and a width control the drawing layer would not.
    plots: [
      { key: 'zigzag', type: 'line', title: 'Zig Zag', style: { color: ZIGZAG_COLOR, lineWidth: 1 } },
    ],

    calc(bars, settings, store, ctx) {
      const n = bars.length
      // A cleared field arrives as '', and Number('') is 0. Pine's minval is 2.
      const period = Math.max(2, Math.floor(Number(settings.zzPeriod) // 4))
      const useOpenClose = settings.zzSource === 'Open/Close'
      const showZigzag = settings.showZigzag !== false
      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      // A dropdown in Pine always holds one of its options; a cleared select here
      // does not, so fall back to the default rather than drawing nothing.
      const method = METHODS.includes(settings.method) ? settings.method : METHODS[1]

      const zigzagCol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const longSig = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const shortSig = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const levelPrice = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const levelTime = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumPchg = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumVolPchg = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumVol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const prevVol = new Array(n).fill(NaN)

      /* ---- zig zag ------------------------------------------------------ */

      const swingHigh = new Array(n)
      const swingLow = new Array(n)
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const b = bars[i]
        swingHigh[i] = useOpenClose ? Math.max(b.open, b.close) : b.high
        swingLow[i] = useOpenClose ? Math.min(b.open, b.close) : b.low
      }
      // ta.highestbars(...) == 0 means this bar is the highest of the window, so
      // the pivot is known on the bar itself and never repaints backwards. Both
      // helpers hold NaN for the first period-1 bars, exactly as Pine holds na,
      // and both resolve a tie to the most recent bar, which is what Pine does.
      const hiBars = highestBars(swingHigh, period)
      const loBars = lowestBars(swingLow, period)

      // The Pine array is a flat [value, barIndex, ...] stack, newest pair first,
      // trimmed to seven points. Kept literally, because zz_1 .. zz_7 below are
      // read by offset from its END and those offsets shift while it fills.
      const MAX_ARRAY_SIZE = 14
      const zigzag = []
      // The same points in chronological order, for the legs the source draws.
      const points = []
      let dir = 0

      const addPoint = (value, index) => {
        zigzag.unshift(index)
        zigzag.unshift(value)
        if (zigzag.length > MAX_ARRAY_SIZE) {
          zigzag.pop()
          zigzag.pop()
        }
        points.push({ value, index })
      }

      const at = (k) => (k >= 0 && k < zigzag.length ? zigzag[k] : NaN)

      const zz1 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz2 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz3 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz4 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz5 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz6 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const zz7 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const bi3 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const bi5 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const bi7 = new Array(n).fill(NaN)

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const ph = hiBars[i] === 0 ? swingHigh[i] : NaN
        const pl = loBars[i] === 0 ? swingLow[i] : NaN
        const hasPh = Number.isFinite(ph)
        const hasPl = Number.isFinite(pl)

        // dir flips only when exactly one side prints: a bar that is both the
        // window high and the window low leaves the direction alone.
        const prevDir = dir
        if (hasPl && !hasPh) dir = -1
        else if (hasPh && !hasPl) dir = 1
        const dirChanged = dir !== prevDir

        if (hasPh // hasPl) {
          const value = dir === 1 ? ph : pl
          if (Number.isFinite(value)) {
            if (dirChanged) {
              addPoint(value, i)
            } else if (zigzag.length === 0) {
              addPoint(value, i)
            } else if ((dir === 1 && value > zigzag[0]) // (dir === -1 && value < zigzag[0])) {
              // The swing in progress extends: move the newest point, do not add.
              zigzag[0] = value
              zigzag[1] = i
              points[points.length - 1] = { value, index: i }
            }
          }
        }

        // Read verbatim from the source, including the offsets it uses while the
        // stack is still filling, where zz_1 is na and zz_2 holds the newest point.
        const size = zigzag.length
        zz1[i] = size > 13 ? at(size - 14) : NaN
        zz2[i] = size > 11 ? at(size - 12) : NaN
        zz3[i] = size > 9 ? at(size - 10) : NaN
        bi3[i] = size > 8 ? at(size - 9) : NaN
        zz4[i] = size > 7 ? at(size - 8) : NaN
        zz5[i] = size > 5 ? at(size - 6) : NaN
        bi5[i] = size > 4 ? at(size - 5) : NaN
        zz6[i] = size > 3 ? at(size - 4) : NaN
        zz7[i] = size > 1 ? at(size - 2) : NaN
        bi7[i] = size > 0 ? at(size - 1) : NaN
      }

      if (showZigzag) {
        // One leg per consecutive pair of points. The source only starts drawing
        // once three points exist, so its very first leg is never painted; that
        // is reproduced here rather than quietly improved.
        for (let k = 1; k + 1 < points.length; k++) {
          const a = points[k]
          const b = points[k + 1]
          const span = b.index - a.index
          if (!(span > 0)) {
            zigzagCol[b.index] = b.value
            continue
          }
          for (let i = a.index; i <= b.index; i++) {
            zigzagCol[i] = a.value + ((b.value - a.value) * (i - a.index)) / span
          }
        }
      }

      /* ---- sweep conditions --------------------------------------------- */

      const crossOver = (a, b, i) =>
        i > 0 &&
        Number.isFinite(a[i]) && Number.isFinite(b[i]) &&
        Number.isFinite(a[i - 1]) && Number.isFinite(b[i - 1]) &&
        a[i] > b[i] && a[i - 1] <= b[i - 1]

      const crossUnder = (a, b, i) =>
        i > 0 &&
        Number.isFinite(a[i]) && Number.isFinite(b[i]) &&
        Number.isFinite(a[i - 1]) && Number.isFinite(b[i - 1]) &&
        a[i] < b[i] && a[i - 1] >= b[i - 1]

      // The seven-swing shape the source demands, transcribed comparison for
      // comparison. a..f are zz_2 .. zz_7; zz_1 is the swing doing the sweeping.
      const bearStack = (i) => {
        const a = zz2[i], b = zz3[i], c = zz4[i], d = zz5[i], e = zz6[i], f = zz7[i]
        if (!Number.isFinite(a) // !Number.isFinite(b) // !Number.isFinite(c)) return false
        if (!Number.isFinite(d) // !Number.isFinite(e) // !Number.isFinite(f)) return false
        return (
          a < b && a < c && a < e && a < f &&
          b < d && b > c && b > a &&
          c < b && c < d && c < e && c < f &&
          d > b && d > c && d > e && d < f &&
          e < d && e < f && e > c &&
          f > a && f > b && f > c && f > d && f > e
        )
      }

      const bullStack = (i) => {
        const a = zz2[i], b = zz3[i], c = zz4[i], d = zz5[i], e = zz6[i], f = zz7[i]
        if (!Number.isFinite(a) // !Number.isFinite(b) // !Number.isFinite(c)) return false
        if (!Number.isFinite(d) // !Number.isFinite(e) // !Number.isFinite(f)) return false
        return (
          a > b && a > c && a > e && a > f &&
          b > d && b < c && b < a &&
          c > b && c > d && c > e && c > f &&
          d < b && d < c && d < e && d > f &&
          e > d && e > f && e < c &&
          f < a && f < b && f < c && f < d && f < e
        )
      }

      // barstate.isconfirmed: every loaded bar is closed except, on a live feed,
      // the last one. Without a context, treat the series as history.
      const lastIndex = n - 1
      const lastConfirmed = ctx?.barState?.isConfirmed !== false

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (i === lastIndex && !lastConfirmed) continue
        const bear = bearStack(i)
        const bull = bullStack(i)

        let shortHit = false
        let longHit = false
        let price = NaN
        let fromBar = NaN

        if (method === METHODS[0]) {
          shortHit = bear && crossOver(zz1, zz3, i)
          // Verbatim from the source: long_condition_1 tests the SAME stack the
          // short conditions test, unlike long_condition_2 and _3 which mirror it.
          longHit = bear && crossUnder(zz1, zz3, i)
          price = zz3[i]
          fromBar = bi3[i]
        } else if (method === METHODS[1]) {
          shortHit = bear && crossOver(zz1, zz5, i)
          longHit = bull && crossUnder(zz1, zz5, i)
          price = zz5[i]
          fromBar = bi5[i]
        } else {
          shortHit = bear && crossOver(zz1, zz7, i)
          longHit = bull && crossUnder(zz1, zz7, i)
          price = zz7[i]
          fromBar = bi7[i]
        }

        const shortOn = showShort && shortHit
        const longOn = showLong && longHit
        if (shortOn) shortSig[i] = 1
        if (longOn) longSig[i] = 1

        if (shortOn // longOn) {
          const anchor = Math.trunc(fromBar)
          if (Number.isFinite(price) && Number.isFinite(anchor) && anchor >= 0 && anchor < n) {
            levelPrice[i] = price
            levelTime[i] = bars[anchor].time
          }
        }
      }

      /* ---- per-day accumulators behind the data table -------------------- */

      const zoneSetting = ctx?.timezone
      const zone =
        typeof zoneSetting === 'string' && zoneSetting !== '' && isValidTimezone(zoneSetting)
          ? zoneSetting
          : DEFAULT_TIMEZONE
      const newDay = calendarPeriodFlags(bars.map((b) => b.time), (a, b) => isNewZonedDay(a, b, zone))

      let runningPct = NaN
      let dayVol = NaN
      let priorDayVol = NaN
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        // The first loaded bar opens the first day: Pine has no previous daily
        // stamp to compare against there either, and seeding the day keeps the
        // volume total from staying na until the first boundary.
        const isNewDay = i === 0 // newDay[i] === true
        const prevClose = i > 0 ? bars[i - 1].close : NaN
        const close = bars[i].close
        const barPct =
          Number.isFinite(prevClose) && prevClose !== 0 && Number.isFinite(close)
            ? ((close - prevClose) / prevClose) * 100
            : 0
        runningPct = isNewDay ? barPct : Number.isFinite(runningPct) ? runningPct + barPct : barPct
        cumPchg[i] = runningPct

        // Volume is genuinely missing on index series, so it counts as nothing
        // rather than poisoning the whole day's total.
        const vol = Number.isFinite(bars[i].volume) ? bars[i].volume : 0
        if (isNewDay) {
          priorDayVol = dayVol
          dayVol = vol
        } else {
          dayVol = (Number.isFinite(dayVol) ? dayVol : 0) + vol
        }
        cumVol[i] = dayVol
        prevVol[i] = priorDayVol

        // nz(prev, current): with no previous day the change against itself is 0.
        const base = Number.isFinite(priorDayVol) ? priorDayVol : dayVol
        cumVolPchg[i] =
          Number.isFinite(base) && base !== 0 && Number.isFinite(dayVol)
            ? ((dayVol - base) / base) * 100
            : NaN
      }

      return {
        zigzag: nulls(zigzagCol),
        longSig: nulls(longSig),
        shortSig: nulls(shortSig),
        levelPrice: nulls(levelPrice),
        levelTime: nulls(levelTime),
        cumPchg: nulls(cumPchg),
        cumVolPchg: nulls(cumVolPchg),
        cumVol: nulls(cumVol),
        prevVol: nulls(prevVol),
      }
    },

    // plotshape(location.abovebar / belowbar). On an overlay those anchor to this
    // indicator's own line, so the triangles are placed at an explicit price with
    // a pad scaled to the instrument's own bar range.
    markers({ bars, values }) {
      const out = []
      if (bars.length === 0) return out

      let sum = 0
      let count = 0
      for (const b of bars) {
        const range = b.high - b.low
        if (Number.isFinite(range)) {
          sum += range
          count += 1
        }
      }
      const meanRange = count > 0 ? sum / count : 0
      const lastClose = bars[bars.length - 1].close
      const pad = Math.max(meanRange * 0.5, Math.abs(Number.isFinite(lastClose) ? lastClose : 0) * 0.0005, 1e-8)

      for (let i = 0; i < bars.length; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        if (values.shortSig[i] === 1 && Number.isFinite(bar.high)) {
          out.push({
            time: bar.time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bar.high + pad,
            shape: 'triangleDown',
            size: 'tiny',
            color: NEG_LIGHT,
          })
        }
        if (values.longSig[i] === 1 && Number.isFinite(bar.low)) {
          out.push({
            time: bar.time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bar.low - pad,
            shape: 'triangleUp',
            size: 'tiny',
            color: POS_LIGHT,
          })
        }
      }
      return out
    },

    // line.new from the swept swing across to the signal bar, at the swing price.
    draws({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const out = []
      if (bars.length === 0) return out
      const lineStyle = LINE_STYLES.includes(settings.levelLineStyle) ? settings.levelLineStyle : 'solid'

      for (let i = 0; i < bars.length; i++) {
        const price = values.levelPrice[i]
        const from = values.levelTime[i]
        if (!Number.isFinite(price) // !Number.isFinite(from)) continue
        out.push({
          kind: 'line',
          from: { time: from, price },
          to: { time: bars[i].time, price },
          color: values.shortSig[i] === 1 ? NEG_MID : POS_MID,
          lineWidth: 1,
          lineStyle,
        })
      }
      return out
    },

    // barcolor(): the short verdict is tested first, exactly as the source does.
    barColors({ bars, values }) {
      return bars.map((b, i) =>
        values.shortSig[i] === 1 ? NEG_LIGHT : values.longSig[i] === 1 ? POS_LIGHT : null
      )
    },

    table({ bars, values, settings }) {
      if (settings.showDataTable === false // bars.length === 0) return null
      const i = bars.length - 1
      const pct = values.cumPchg[i]
      const volPct = values.cumVolPchg[i]
      const vol = values.cumVol[i]
      const priorVol = values.prevVol[i]

      // str.tostring(x, '#.##'): at most two decimals, no trailing zeros.
      const num = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? String(Number(v.toFixed(2))) : '-')
      const lakh = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? String(Number((v / 100000).toFixed(2))) + ' L' : '-')
      const head = (text, bgColor) => ({ text, align: 'left', bgColor, textColor: NEU_LIGHT })
      const cell = (text, bgColor, textColor) => ({ text, align: 'right', bgColor, textColor })

      const pctColor = Number.isFinite(pct) && pct > 0 ? POS_MID : NEG_MID
      const volPctColor = Number.isFinite(volPct) && volPct > 0 ? POS_MID : NEG_MID
      const priorVolColor =
        Number.isFinite(priorVol) && Number.isFinite(vol) && priorVol < vol ? NEG_MID : POS_MID

      const position = TABLE_POSITIONS.includes(settings.tablePosition) ? settings.tablePosition : 'bottom-right'
      const fontSize = FONT_SIZES[settings.tableSize] ?? FONT_SIZES.normal

      return {
        rows: [
          [head('%Chg', NEU_DARK), cell(num(pct) + ' %', NEU_DARK, pctColor)],
          [head('Vol %Chg', NEU_MID), cell(num(volPct) + ' %', NEU_MID, volPctColor)],
          [head('Vol', NEU_DARK), cell(lakh(vol), NEU_DARK, volPctColor)],
          [head('PD Vol | `oa-ict-liquidity-sweep-pattern-scanner` | `oa-ict-liquidity-sweep-pattern-scanner.js` | [source](https://github.com/ArunKBhaskar/PineScript/blob/c6821225c466494b01eee08f9dd88bf84d2b24ba/ICT) |
| ICT Liquidity Void Fill Scanner',

        style: { color: POS_COLOR, lineWidth: 2 },
      },
    ],

    calc(bars, settings, store, ctx) {
      const n = bars.length

      const bearFibLine = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const bullFibLine = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const shortSignal = new Array(n).fill(0)
      const longSignal = new Array(n).fill(0)
      const shortCandle = new Array(n).fill(0)
      const longCandle = new Array(n).fill(0)
      const cumPchg = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const cumVolPchg = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const dayVolume = new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      const prevDayVolume = new Array(n).fill(NaN)

      const empty = {
        bearFibLine: nulls(bearFibLine),
        bullFibLine: nulls(bullFibLine),
        shortSignal,
        longSignal,
        shortCandle,
        longCandle,
        cumPchg: nulls(cumPchg),
        cumVolPchg: nulls(cumVolPchg),
        dayVolume: nulls(dayVolume),
        prevDayVolume: nulls(prevDayVolume),
      }
      if (n === 0) return empty

      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      const fibVal = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, num(settings.fibVal, 0.5)))

      const useAtrFilter = settings.atrFilter !== false
      const atrLength = Math.max(1, Math.floor(num(settings.atrLength, 14)))
      const atrMulti = Math.max(1, num(settings.atrMulti, 1))
      const useBodyFilter = settings.bodyFilter !== false
      const bodyPercent = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, num(settings.bodyPercent, 80))) / 100
      const useBodySizeFilter = settings.bodySizeFilter === true
      const bodySizeMultiplier = Math.max(0, num(settings.bodySizeMultiplier, 2))

      const useTimeFilter = settings.timeFilter === true
      const hourFrom = Math.max(0, Math.floor(num(settings.hourFrom, 9)))
      const minuteFrom = Math.max(0, Math.floor(num(settings.minuteFrom, 15)))
      const hourTo = Math.max(0, Math.floor(num(settings.hourTo, 10)))
      const minuteTo = Math.max(0, Math.floor(num(settings.minuteTo, 15)))

      const useDateFilter = settings.dateFilter === true
      const wantDay = Math.max(1, Math.floor(num(settings.day, 13)))
      const wantMonth = Math.max(1, Math.floor(num(settings.month, 3)))
      const wantYear = Math.max(0, Math.floor(num(settings.year, 2025)))

      const zoneRaw = ctx?.timezone
      const zone =
        typeof zoneRaw === 'string' && zoneRaw !== '' && isValidTimezone(zoneRaw)
          ? zoneRaw
          : DEFAULT_TIMEZONE

      // barstate.isconfirmed: every historical bar is closed, and only the last
      // one can still be forming.
      const lastUnconfirmed = ctx?.barState?.isConfirmed === false

      const high = new Array(n)
      const low = new Array(n)
      const close = new Array(n)
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        high[i] = bars[i].high
        low[i] = bars[i].low
        close[i] = bars[i].close
      }
      const atrValues = atr(high, low, close, atrLength)

      // ta.change(time('D')) != 0. Pine's change is na on the first bar, and
      // na != 0 is false there, so bar 0 never counts as a new day.
      const dayIndex = new Array(n)
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) dayIndex[i] = zonedDayIndex(bars[i].time, zone)

      // Daily cumulative percentage change and daily cumulative volume, both
      // var-carried in Pine. curr_cum_vol starts as na and only becomes a real
      // number at the first day change, which is what the source does.
      let cum = NaN
      let currCumVol = NaN
      let prevCumVol = NaN

      // Displacement candle state, carried by var in Pine.
      let shortHigh = NaN
      let shortLow = NaN
      let shortBar = -1
      let longHigh = NaN
      let longLow = NaN
      let longBar = -1

      let shortState = 0
      let longState = 0

      let prevBearFib = NaN
      let prevBullFib = NaN

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        const isNewDay = i > 0 && dayIndex[i] !== dayIndex[i - 1]

        // Cumulative percentage change of close, reset each day.
        const prevClose = i > 0 ? close[i - 1] : NaN
        const dailyPct =
          Number.isFinite(prevClose) && prevClose !== 0
            ? ((close[i] - prevClose) / prevClose) * 100
            : 0
        cum = isNewDay ? dailyPct : Number.isFinite(cum) ? cum + dailyPct : dailyPct
        cumPchg[i] = cum

        // Cumulative volume, reset each day, previous day kept for comparison.
        const vol = Number.isFinite(bar.volume) ? bar.volume : 0
        if (isNewDay) {
          prevCumVol = currCumVol
          currCumVol = vol
        } else {
          currCumVol = currCumVol + vol
        }
        dayVolume[i] = currCumVol
        prevDayVolume[i] = prevCumVol
        const base = Number.isFinite(prevCumVol) ? prevCumVol : currCumVol
        cumVolPchg[i] =
          Number.isFinite(base) && base !== 0 ? ((currCumVol - base) / base) * 100 : NaN

        // Additional filters on the displacement candle.
        const range = high[i] - low[i]
        const body = Math.abs(close[i] - bar.open)

        let atrOk = true
        if (useAtrFilter) {
          const a = atrValues[i]
          atrOk = Number.isFinite(a) && range > a * atrMulti
        }

        // A zero-range candle makes the body ratio na in Pine, and every
        // comparison with na is false, so it fails the filter rather than
        // dividing by zero here.
        let bodyOk = true
        if (useBodyFilter) bodyOk = range > 0 && body / range >= bodyPercent

        let bodySizeOk = true
        if (useBodySizeFilter) {
          const prevRange = i > 0 ? high[i - 1] - low[i - 1] : NaN
          bodySizeOk =
            range > 0 &&
            body / range >= bodyPercent &&
            Number.isFinite(prevRange) &&
            range >= prevRange * bodySizeMultiplier
        }

        const filtersOk = atrOk && bodyOk && bodySizeOk
        const shortCont1 = bar.open > close[i] && filtersOk
        const longCont1 = bar.open < close[i] && filtersOk
        shortCandle[i] = shortCont1 ? 1 : 0
        longCandle[i] = longCont1 ? 1 : 0

        if (shortCont1) {
          shortHigh = high[i]
          shortLow = low[i]
          shortBar = i
        }
        if (longCont1) {
          longHigh = high[i]
          longLow = low[i]
          longBar = i
        }

        // fibonacci(false, ...) measures down from the high, fibonacci(true, ...)
        // measures up from the low.
        const bearFib = Number.isFinite(shortHigh) ? shortHigh - (shortHigh - shortLow) * fibVal : NaN
        const bullFib = Number.isFinite(longLow) ? longLow + (longHigh - longLow) * fibVal : NaN

        // Filters on the retracement candle.
        let timeOk = true
        let dateOk = true
        if (useTimeFilter // useDateFilter) {
          const parts = utcSecondsToZonedParts(bar.time, zone)
          if (useTimeFilter) {
            const h = parts.hour
            const m = parts.minute
            timeOk =
              (h > hourFrom // (h === hourFrom && m >= minuteFrom)) &&
              (h < hourTo // (h === hourTo && m < minuteTo))
          }
          if (useDateFilter) {
            dateOk = parts.year === wantYear && parts.month === wantMonth && parts.day === wantDay
          }
        }

        const confirmed = !(lastUnconfirmed && i === n - 1)

        // ta.crossover / ta.crossunder. Both sides of both bars must be real
        // numbers, or the warmup gap fires a signal straight through.
        const crossedOverBear =
          Number.isFinite(bearFib) &&
          Number.isFinite(prevBearFib) &&
          i > 0 &&
          Number.isFinite(high[i]) &&
          Number.isFinite(high[i - 1]) &&
          high[i] > bearFib &&
          high[i - 1] <= prevBearFib
        const crossedUnderBull =
          Number.isFinite(bullFib) &&
          Number.isFinite(prevBullFib) &&
          i > 0 &&
          Number.isFinite(low[i]) &&
          Number.isFinite(low[i - 1]) &&
          low[i] < bullFib &&
          low[i - 1] >= prevBullFib

        const shortCont2 = crossedOverBear && timeOk && dateOk && confirmed
        const longCont2 = crossedUnderBull && timeOk && dateOk && confirmed

        // Two-step state machine: arm on the displacement candle, fire on the
        // retracement, then clear on the bar after the signal.
        shortState = shortState === 2 ? 0 : shortState
        if (shortCont1 && shortState === 0) shortState = 1
        if (!shortCont1 && shortCont2 && shortState === 1) shortState = 2

        longState = longState === 2 ? 0 : longState
        if (longCont1 && longState === 0) longState = 1
        if (!longCont1 && longCont2 && longState === 1) longState = 2

        const shortRet = shortState === 2
        const longRet = longState === 2
        shortSignal[i] = shortRet ? 1 : 0
        longSignal[i] = longRet ? 1 : 0

        // line.new from the displacement bar to the signal bar, at the fill
        // level, carried as a filled span of the plot column.
        if (showShort && shortRet && shortBar >= 0 && Number.isFinite(bearFib)) {
          for (let j = shortBar; j <= i; j++) bearFibLine[j] = bearFib
        }
        if (showLong && longRet && longBar >= 0 && Number.isFinite(bullFib)) {
          for (let j = longBar; j <= i; j++) bullFibLine[j] = bullFib
        }

        prevBearFib = bearFib
        prevBullFib = bullFib
      }

      return {
        bearFibLine: nulls(bearFibLine),
        bullFibLine: nulls(bullFibLine),
        shortSignal,
        longSignal,
        shortCandle,
        longCandle,
        cumPchg: nulls(cumPchg),
        cumVolPchg: nulls(cumVolPchg),
        dayVolume: nulls(dayVolume),
        prevDayVolume: nulls(prevDayVolume),
      }
    },

    // plotshape at location.abovebar / location.belowbar. aboveBar and belowBar
    // would anchor to this indicator's own line, so the offset is computed here
    // and scaled to the instrument.
    markers({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const n = bars.length
      if (n === 0) return []
      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      if (!showLong && !showShort) return []

      let rangeSum = 0
      let rangeCount = 0
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const r = bars[i].high - bars[i].low
        if (Number.isFinite(r) && r > 0) {
          rangeSum += r
          rangeCount++
        }
      }
      const meanRange = rangeCount > 0 ? rangeSum / rangeCount : 0
      const lastClose = Number.isFinite(bars[n - 1].close) ? bars[n - 1].close : 0
      const pad = Math.max(meanRange * 0.5, Math.abs(lastClose) * 0.0005, 0)

      const shortSignal = values.shortSignal
      const longSignal = values.longSignal
      const out = []
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (showShort && shortSignal[i] === 1 && Number.isFinite(bars[i].high)) {
          out.push({
            time: bars[i].time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bars[i].high + pad,
            shape: 'triangleDown',
            size: 'tiny',
            color: NEG_LIGHT_COLOR,
          })
        }
        if (showLong && longSignal[i] === 1 && Number.isFinite(bars[i].low)) {
          out.push({
            time: bars[i].time,
            position: 'atPrice',
            price: bars[i].low - pad,
            shape: 'triangleUp',
            size: 'tiny',
            color: POS_LIGHT_COLOR,
          })
        }
      }
      return out
    },

    // barcolor(): the displacement candle itself, short tested first as in Pine.
    barColors({ bars, values, settings }) {
      const showLong = settings.showLong !== false
      const showShort = settings.showShort !== false
      const shortCandle = values.shortCandle
      const longCandle = values.longCandle
      return bars.map((bar, i) => {
        if (showShort && shortCandle[i] === 1) return NEG_LIGHT_COLOR
        if (showLong && longCandle[i] === 1) return POS_LIGHT_COLOR
        return null
      })
    },

    // The source's own data table: day change, volume change and the two
    // cumulative volumes, read from the last bar.
    table({ bars, values, settings }) {
      if (settings.showDataTable === false) return null
      const n = bars.length
      if (n === 0) return null
      const i = n - 1
      const pchg = values.cumPchg[i]
      const volPchg = values.cumVolPchg[i]
      const vol = values.dayVolume[i]
      const prevVol = values.prevDayVolume[i]
      const lakhs = (v) => (Number.isFinite(v) ? `${fmt2(v / 100000)} L` : 'na')
      return {
        rows: [
          ['%Chg', `${fmt2(pchg)} %`],
          ['Vol %Chg', `${fmt2(volPchg)} %`],
          ['Vol', lakhs(vol)],
          ['PD Vol | `oa-ict-liquidity-void-fill-scanner-scanner` | `oa-ict-liquidity-void-fill-scanner-scanner.js` | [source](https://github.com/ArunKBhaskar/PineScript/blob/c6821225c466494b01eee08f9dd88bf84d2b24ba/ICT) |
| ICT Liquidity Void Fill',
    category: 'ICT',
    placement: 'onchart',

      { key: 'showShort', type: 'boolean', label: 'Short Signals', default: true, group: 'Liquidity Void' },
      {

      { key: 'atrMulti', type: 'number', label: 'ATR Multiplier', default: 1, min: 1, max: 100, step: 0.1, group: 'Additional Filters' },

      {

      { key: 'minuteFrom', type: 'number', label: 'Time From (minute)', default: 15, min: 0, max: 59, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'hourTo', type: 'number', label: 'Time To (hour)', default: 10, min: 0, max: 23, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'minuteTo', type: 'number', label: 'Time To (minute)', default: 15, min: 0, max: 59, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },

      {
        key: 'dateFilter',
        type: 'boolean',
        label: 'Apply Date Filter',

      },
      { key: 'day', type: 'number', label: 'Day', default: 13, min: 1, max: 31, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'month', type: 'number', label: 'Month', default: 3, min: 1, max: 12, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
      { key: 'year', type: 'number', label: 'Year', default: 2025, min: 0, max: 9999, step: 1, group: 'Additional Filters' },
    ],

    // The source plots nothing: it draws shapes, bar colours and lines. These two
    // columns are the bear_fib_val and bull_fib_val series it computes on every
    // bar, declared as hidden plots so they are available without changing the
    // picture. Turn either on from the plot style controls to see the level.
    plots: [
      { key: 'bearFib', type: 'line', title: 'Bearish Void Level', style: { color: NEG_COLOR, lineWidth: 1, visible: false } },
      { key: 'bullFib', type: 'line', title: 'Bullish Void Level', style: { color: POS_COLOR, lineWidth: 1, visible: false } },
    ],

    calc(bars, settings, store, ctx) {
      const n = bars.length
      const blank = () => new Array(n).fill(NaN)
      if (n === 0) {
        return {
          bearFib: nulls(blank()),
          bullFib: nulls(blank()),
          shortSignal: nulls(blank()),
          longSignal: nulls(blank()),
          shortCont1: nulls(blank()),
          longCont1: nulls(blank()),
          shortAnchorTime: nulls(blank()),
          longAnchorTime: nulls(blank()),
        }
      }

      const fibValue = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, num(settings.fibValue, 0.5)))
      const useAtr = settings.atrFilter !== false
      const atrLength = Math.max(1, int(settings.atrLength, 14))
      const atrMulti = Math.max(1, num(settings.atrMulti, 1))
      const useBody = settings.bodyFilter !== false
      // Pine divides the 0 to 100 input by 100 the moment it reads it.
      const bodyPercent = Math.min(100, Math.max(0, num(settings.bodyPercent, 80))) / 100
      const useBodySize = settings.bodySizeFilter === true
      const bodySizeMultiplier = Math.max(0, num(settings.bodySizeMultiplier, 2))
      const useTime = settings.timeFilter === true
      const hourFrom = Math.max(0, int(settings.hourFrom, 9))
      const minuteFrom = Math.max(0, int(settings.minuteFrom, 15))
      const hourTo = Math.max(0, int(settings.hourTo, 10))
      const minuteTo = Math.max(0, int(settings.minuteTo, 15))
      const useDate = settings.dateFilter === true
      const wantDay = Math.max(1, int(settings.day, 13))
      const wantMonth = Math.max(1, int(settings.month, 3))
      const wantYear = Math.max(0, int(settings.year, 2025))

      // Pine's hour, minute, year, month and dayofmonth are exchange wall clock,
      // never the viewer's machine clock.
      const candidate = settings.timezone ?? ctx?.timezone ?? DEFAULT_TIMEZONE
      const zone = isValidTimezone(candidate) ? candidate : DEFAULT_TIMEZONE

      const high = bars.map((b) => b.high)
      const low = bars.map((b) => b.low)
      const close = bars.map((b) => b.close)
      const atrSeries = useAtr ? atr(high, low, close, atrLength) : null

      // barstate.isconfirmed: every historical bar is confirmed, and the last one
      // is only unconfirmed while a live bar is still forming.
      const liveUnconfirmed = ctx?.barState?.isRealtime === true && ctx?.barState?.isConfirmed !== true

      const bearFib = blank()
      const bullFib = blank()
      const shortSignal = blank()
      const longSignal = blank()
      const shortCont1Col = blank()
      const longCont1Col = blank()
      const shortAnchorTime = blank()
      const longAnchorTime = blank()

      // var-carried anchors: the most recent displacement candle of each side.
      let shortHigh = NaN
      let shortLow = NaN
      let shortAnchor = -1
      let longHigh = NaN
      let longLow = NaN
      let longAnchor = -1

      let shortState = 0
      let longState = 0

      let prevBearFib = NaN
      let prevBullFib = NaN

      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const bar = bars[i]
        const o = bar.open
        const h = bar.high
        const l = bar.low
        const c = bar.close
        const range = h - l
        const ok = Number.isFinite(o) && Number.isFinite(h) && Number.isFinite(l) && Number.isFinite(c)

        // Additional filters. Each defaults to true and only narrows when on.
        let atrPass = true
        if (useAtr) {
          const a = atrSeries[i]
          // ta.atr is na through its warmup, and every comparison with na is
          // false in Pine, so the filter blocks rather than passes there.
          atrPass = ok && Number.isFinite(a) && range > a * atrMulti
        }

        let bodyPass = true
        if (useBody) {
          // A zero-range bar makes this 0/0, which is na in Pine and so false.
          bodyPass = ok && range > 0 && Math.abs(c - o) / range >= bodyPercent
        }

        let bodySizePass = true
        if (useBodySize) {
          const prevRange = i > 0 ? bars[i - 1].high - bars[i - 1].low : NaN
          bodySizePass =
            ok &&
            range > 0 &&
            Math.abs(c - o) / range >= bodyPercent &&
            Number.isFinite(prevRange) &&
            range >= prevRange * bodySizeMultiplier
        }

        let timePass = true
        if (useTime) {
          const parts = utcSecondsToZonedParts(bar.time, zone)
          const hour = parts.hour
          const minute = parts.minute
          // Pine binds `and` tighter than `or`.
          timePass =
            (hour > hourFrom // (hour === hourFrom && minute >= minuteFrom)) &&
            (hour < hourTo // (hour === hourTo && minute < minuteTo))
        }

        let datePass = true
        if (useDate) {
          const parts = utcSecondsToZonedParts(bar.time, zone)
          datePass = parts.year === wantYear && parts.month === wantMonth && parts.day === wantDay
        }

        const confirmed = i < n - 1 // !liveUnconfirmed
        const filtersPass = atrPass && bodyPass && bodySizePass

        // Displacement candles.
        const shortCont1 = ok && o > c && filtersPass
        const longCont1 = ok && o < c && filtersPass

        if (shortCont1) {
          shortHigh = h
          shortLow = l
          shortAnchor = i
        }
        if (longCont1) {
          longHigh = h
          longLow = l
          longAnchor = i
        }

        // fibonacci(false, ...) measures down from the high of a bearish candle,
        // fibonacci(true, ...) measures up from the low of a bullish one.
        const bear =
